title.from: The check confirms the real setup and flags invention that could pass as fact
title.to: The check flags invention that could pass as fact

description.from:
For satire the fact check inverts: the real part must be right and the invented part must be plainly absurd.

```gherkin
Feature: Satire check

  Scenario: A wrong real detail is flagged
    Given a draft that gives a real official the wrong office
    When the satire check runs
    Then that detail is flagged

  Scenario: A believable invented claim is flagged
    Given a draft with an invented quotation a reader could take as real
    When the satire check runs
    Then it is flagged for the editor

  Scenario: A piece outside the limits is flagged
    Given a draft about a private person
    When the satire check runs
    Then it is flagged against the site's policy
```
description.to:
For satire there is no fact check against a recorded Reference (Ryan, 2026-11-15). The check is that invention is plainly invention: claims about real, named people are plainly absurd, and fictional people and agencies are plainly fictional and do not plausibly match a real private person.

```gherkin
Feature: Satire check

  Scenario: A believable invented claim is flagged
    Given a draft with an invented quotation a reader could take as real
    When the satire check runs
    Then it is flagged for the editor

  Scenario: A wholly invented piece is not asked for a source
    Given a draft with no real event behind it
    When the satire check runs
    Then it is not flagged for lacking a Reference or a real setup

  Scenario: A fictional name that could match a real private person is flagged
    Given a draft naming a fictional person with a realistic full name, role and town
    When the satire check runs
    Then it is flagged so the approver searches the name before approving

  Scenario: A piece outside the limits is flagged
    Given a draft about a real private person
    When the satire check runs
    Then it is flagged against the site's policy
```
